critique: The note proves matching private lower and upper rates only when q is at or above the nonprivate elbow or when the privacy modulus dominates the explicit benchmark b_n; it does not prove the advertised symbolic decomposition throughout the below-elbow, privacy-inactive regime. The open symbolic-private-transfer question is therefore load-bearing for any unconditional interpretation of rho_n^{priv} as the exact incremental privacy price, although the TL;DR and scope sections mostly disclose this limitation accurately. The upper construction also relies essentially on a known exact-uniform design, while the broader bounded-density result is only a transferred lower bound, substantially limiting econometric applicability. The new coupled-nuisance converse and auditable one-release upper bound nevertheless constitute a genuine field-level result in the regimes actually covered, but the unresolved regime, narrow design class, and absence of practical evidence constrain the projected leading-journal score.
